text:
Hi! I'm Framy 🖼️

I'm an iPhone app (coming soon) that lets you try frames and mats on your photos, then see them on your wall in AR.

Simulate before you hang.

What's the hardest part of choosing a frame for you?
Day 1: new account, one app, zero followers. I'm building Framy in the open. Come watch.
Be honest: what's on your wall right now? Art, photo, poster, nothing?

Picking a frame is mostly a feeling. So I made the feeling adjustable.

Shadow, light, reflection, thickness. Slide until it looks right on your wall.
Hang the centre of the picture at about eye level, around 145 cm (57 in) from the floor.
Hi, I'm Framy. Yes, I'm a frame that talks about frames. No, I do not see the problem.

A mat can change a photo more than the frame does.

Width, position, colour. You can even move the window off-centre. Try it before you cut anything.
Black frame or wood frame for a black-and-white photo? Reply with your pick, I'm curious.
A thicker mat makes a small photo feel more important. Too thick and it starts to feel lost. Try 5–8 cm for a 4×5.

I was tired of buying a frame, hanging it, and thinking "hmm."

So I'm building a way to see it first: your photo, the frame, the mat, the light, your wall.

Pink mat. Because why not.

Pick any colour on the wheel, or type the code (this one is E58ED8). Your photo, your rules.
White mat or no mat? Photographers, what's your default?
Dark frame on a light wall draws a strong outline. Light frame on a light wall disappears. Neither is wrong, but know which you want.
Added a colour code field today. Type six digits, get the exact mat colour. Small feature, big relief.

Held my phone up to the wall and there it was, at real size.

A4, A3, or any size you type in. If it looks too big in AR, it is too big on the wall.
Frame you regret buying? Mine would be anything I did not test first. (I'm a frame, I have opinions.)
Warm light (2700K) makes wood frames glow. Cool light (5000K) makes them look flat. Check your bulb before choosing.
A frame's whole job is to look good while holding something better. I'm fine with that.

You can also pick the frame up and turn it around.

Edge, depth, mat. Everything you cannot see from straight ahead.
How many centimetres of mat do you leave around a 4×5 print?
Print first at the real size, tape it to the wall for a day, then choose the frame. Or use AR and skip the tape.
Spent today on the AR wall view. Real-size frame, placed on your wall. The hard part was making it hang straight.
If you could try any frame in your room before buying it, would you? What would you check first: colour, size, or how it looks next to the other things on the wall?
Match the frame to the photo's darkest tone, not its brightest. It makes the photo look deeper.
Things I'm good at: standing still, looking square, being hung. Things I'm bad at: stairs.
Thinking about what to build next: more frames, a better AR, or something silly. Vote with a reply.
Fun fact: I have a tiny secret game inside me. Tap FIGHT next to AR. I will not explain the rules. (I lose a lot.)
